_comment: TIE NEGATIVE CONTROL -- not signoff evidence. gf180-bandgap#526.
erc-supply-spec.json's item-11 tie verdict is 'zero erc.missing_tie,
from ties the run actually checked' (no degenerate_tap_declaration /
degenerate_well_assertion in erc_coverage.skipped[]). Like the supply
zero, that zero is only meaningful if the rule that produces it can
fire: a ties[] entry whose tap narrowing silently matched nothing would
report exactly the same clean result. This spec is the control that
tells those two cases apart, for every tap class.
It is erc-supply-spec.json verbatim -- same stackup, same vias, same
nets[], same ties[] geometry declarations -- with ONE edit: each of the
three ties[].net values is flipped (vdd <-> vss). The taps drawn in
this layout strap each well class to its REAL rail, so asking for the
other rail must report every class untied:
erc.missing_tie  layer='nwell_tap_pmos'  net='vss'   (1 finding:
the one PMOS-band well region)
erc.missing_tie  layer='nwell_base_pnp'  net='vdd'   (8 findings:
one per vertical-PNP base island)
erc.missing_tie  layer='psub_tap'        net='vdd'   (1 finding:
the one substrate region)
erc_finding_count: 10, all erc.missing_tie, nothing else
status: violations, exit 3
and run_erc.py --expect findings asserts at least one finding. The
per-class identities above are what the committed report actually
carries (its findings name the ties[] entry in `layer`); a class that
stopped firing would mean the rule no longer reaches that class, and
the signoff report's zero for it would have stopped meaning anything --
the item-11 claim must be withdrawn until that is explained.
vdd/vss/vref nets[] entries are carried unchanged, so the control also
demonstrates the supply-island verdicts still hold while the tie
question fails: findings name only the flipped tie nets, and zero
erc.supply_short / erc.unconnected_net are reported alongside.
